Hi Alicia — great to meet you. High level we can offer three pragmatic commitment profiles tailored to early production: Pilot, Baseline, and Anchored. Below is a short summary and next steps; Ben and Marissa are looped for technical sizing and commercial terms.

Summary of options (short):
- Pilot: 8 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs, 4-week warm window, burst to shared-hosted for spikes. Low monthly commitment, quick activation (2–3 weeks).
- Baseline: 32 dedicated GPUs (min-guarantee), staged ramp to 64 across 3 months. Includes hot-swap burst pool and 99th percentile latency SLO for pinned model. Ideal for predictable mid-size production.
- Anchored: 64 dedicated GPUs minimum, 12-month commit with monthly activation cadence to reach 128 in 6 months. Includes reserved burst lanes, extended warm cache pre-warming, and prioritized failover.

Key guardrails and tools:
- Warm-start: KV-cache priming windows we recommend 24–72 hours prior to major launches.
- Burst path: automated routing to compatible quantized variants on shared pool when reserved capacity saturated.
- Fallbacks: canary model rollbacks and automatic throttles to protect SLOs.

What we need from you to firm numbers: expected token/sec at peak, percent of long-context requests (>8k tokens), and target 95/99 latency SLOs. If procurement prefers a multi-tranche financial profile we can send a workbook and sample contract language.

I attached a first-pass pricing workbook (ri_gpu_slate_pricing_v3.xlsx) and an activation timeline doc. Marissa — can you add a financial note and proposed credit for the pilot? Ben — please add a short note on sequence-length sensitivity and recommended min GPU counts per workload.

Next steps: Alicia — if you can confirm the three workload items above by EOD Monday we’ll circulate a formal options sheet for procurement.

Best,
Rishi

Alicia / team — below are technical sizing assumptions I used to map your growth into GPU counts. Pulled from our runtime performance profiles.

Assumptions:
- Chat model: 8k context max for summarization flows; typical request 2–3k tokens.
- Average tokens per response: 450 tokens.
- Concurrent users conversion: at 220 concurrent peak => ~110 qps (estimating half active at response time).
- Effective throughput: one A100-equivalent GPU at our runtime (quantized) supports ~25 qps on chat workloads with 2–3k tokens at 95% latency SLO. Long-context requests reduce throughput by ~35%.

Sizing recommendations (conservative):
- Pilot: 8 GPUs — supports ~200 qps of short chat or ~125 qps of long-context. Good for user testing and load characterization.
- Baseline: 32 GPUs min-guarantee — supports ~800 qps short-chat baseline, with headroom for growth and a staged bump to 64 across month 1–3. If 40% of traffic is long-context, plan for earlier step to 48.
- Anchored: 64 GPUs guaranteed — handles sustained higher concurrency and better headroom for caching benefits; recommended if you plan to A/B multiple large models concurrently.

Notes on ramp schedule and cache warm-up:
- Cache hit improvement: expect 15–35% token-cost reduction after 2 weeks of warm traffic as KV cache stabilizes.
- Activation lead time: 10–21 days for dedicated cluster allocation depending on region and GPU availability at time of activation.
- Burst behaviour: configure burst policy to allow 20–30% overflow into shared pools; latency SLOs drop gracefully with model quantization.

I can run a quick simulation if you can share a 24h sample traffic trace or token histogram.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
